restoration_note: This teaching has two halves with very different restorability profiles. The first half (Sections 5505–5535) is an enumeration of the cosmic supports holding the natural mind in being — Pherokatochos, Great Mind, Jesus the Youth beneath the Mind, twelve and twenty-two angels, seven pillars standing fast, the encircling sea, four bearing-angels stretched to heaven, three great pillars and three Omophoroi under the paiskos, twelve likenesses standing on their feet, firmaments placed by the Living Spirit, seeds sown in them, the perfection of the ten — but most line-openings and line-ends are physically lost (rubbed or destroyed) with no traces, so high-confidence fills are limited to where idioms or single Coptic words are constrained: ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ for the Youth's overhead, ⲣⲉⲧϩ in ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗, ⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ for the surrounding sea, ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ for the four, ⲡⲓⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ for the Living Spirit, ⲃⲣⲣⲉ for what is sown, the editor's ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ/ⲡⲁⲓⲥⲕⲟⲥ/ⲕⲉϣⲁⲙⲧ chain, ⲉⲓⲛⲉ for the likenesses. The second half (5536–5558) on the Yes/Amen and the Calling/Hearing as those who reign over the Aeons of lordship until the soul is mingled with Death and become helpers of the First Man in his ascent — is far better preserved and the editor's restorations (ⲡⲍⲁⲙⲏⲛ, ⲯⲩⲭⲏ, ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ̄, ⲃⲟⲏⲑⲟⲥ, ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄, ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ) are tightly constrained by formula and accepted in full. Across the teaching 52 of 94 gaps are restored; 42 remain unrestorable, almost all in the rubbed or destroyed line-ends of the first half.
